_README: TARGETS/baibai/spec.json — artifact the protocol loop turns on. Sections close only with evidence. A section with an empty evidence field is OPEN.

target.name: BaiBai
target.product: PropAMM exchange + aggregator. PropAMM quotes from its own pricing logic/inventory; aggregates Uniswap/Aerodrome etc. Built on 'Pylon', an appchain framework, synchronously composable with Base (L2 <-> L3 split).

source.verified: PARTIAL — see per-contract 'verified' flags. Two independent registries checked plus one control.
source.route: Blockscout v2 API base.blockscout.com/api/v2/smart-contracts/<addr> + Sourcify sourcify.dev/server/v2/contract/8453/<addr>. Basescan NOT readable (Cloudflare JS challenge) and not defeated by design.
source.note: The three Base contracts that matter for user funds are EIP-1967 proxies whose IMPLEMENTATIONS have no published source in either readable registry. The L2 contracts' implementations ARE verified, which proves the registries index this project correctly and makes the absence meaningful rather than an indexing artefact.

target.coverage_gap: SEVEN published L3 addresses (L3Bridge, TokenFactory, Registry, Router, L3RouterWrapper, Oracle, VaultFactory, L3BaibaiAdmin) are entirely unmapped: no code size, no impl resolution, no verification status, no source. Until mapped, no verdict on this target is permitted by the protocol.

integrations.name: Base settlement (chain 8453)
integrations.notes: L2 contracts live here; users hold normal Base balances, no bridging required per docs.

integrations.name: Pylon appchain (L3)
integrations.notes: Handles market-maker updates and execution logic. 'The appchain remains entirely behind the scenes.' Synchronous composability with Base. Opaque by design — sequence/ordering decisions live off the audited surface.

integrations.name: External aggregators / DEXs (Uniswap, Aerodrome)
integrations.notes: Routing compares PropAMM vs external sources; a manipulation of the comparison is a pricing finding.

integrations.name: Maker order API (Hyperliquid-compatible)
integrations.notes: Makers place/modify/cancel orders via Hyperliquid-compatible endpoints; API wallets + signing + nonces documented (docs/makers/authentication.md). Signature surface.

integrations.name: Gasless swap REST API
integrations.notes: quote -> sign -> submit flow (docs/developers/aggregators-integration.md). The money layer for wallet/aggregator integrations.

assumptions.statement: The three Base implementations are upgradeable by a 1-of-3 Safe, so 'the contracts are audited' does not bind future behaviour.
assumptions.breaks_if: any single owner key is compromised or acts maliciously; the audited/observed logic is replaced.

assumptions.statement: Docs describe 0x98c1D9E1.. / 0x604d9b9e.. / 0xAaC48FEB.. only as 'Verified proxy address' and never disclose that an owner exists or that the logic is upgradeable.
assumptions.breaks_if: users grant a token allowance to the Entrypoint believing its logic is fixed.

assumptions.statement: The L3 appchain is trusted to make routing/ordering decisions that the L2 surface cannot verify.
assumptions.breaks_if: appchain sequencing is compromised or operator-favourable.

assumptions.statement: Custodian.withdrawDelay() = 600s (10 min) is the maker withdrawal reservation window.
assumptions.breaks_if: a maker cannot exit within the disclosed semantics, or the delay is owner-mutable without disclosure.

invariants.statement: swap reverts entirely if minAmountOut is not met, and never partially fills

Any address other than the owner can call upgradeToAndCall on Entrypoint/CurveBook/Custodian

A maker can withdraw more than their credited inventory, or exit outside withdrawDelay

status.blocked_on: nothing (public-surface only). A fork-attack phase needs a Base RPC with headroom — public endpoints 429 under load (rotate: llamarpc / publicnode / 1rpc / drpc).

findings.title: All three user-facing Base contracts are UUPS-upgradeable by a single-signer Safe, and the docs disclose none of it
findings.severity: Medium (centralisation / transparency) — NOT an exploitable bug
findings.impact: A single signer (1-of-3 Safe) can replace the logic of the swap Entrypoint (the token approval target) and the Custodian (maker inventory) at will, bypassing the audited behaviour.
findings.likelihood: Requires owner malicious action or one key compromise; permitted by the design.
findings.evidence: eth_call owner() on all three proxies = 0xb1f4e4d6..; that address is a Safe (masterCopy 0x29fcb43b..) with getThreshold()=1 and 3 owners; upgradeToAndCall/UPGRADE_INTERFACE_VERSION/proxiableUUID present in all three impl bytecodes; implementations unverified in Blockscout AND Sourcify; docs mention only 'Verified proxy address'.

findings.title: Implementations of all three Base contracts have no published source
findings.impact: Classic source review is impossible for the contracts that hold user approvals and maker inventory; every finding on them is bytecode/black-box derived.
findings.evidence: Blockscout v2 returns bytecode-only (no abi/compiler_version/source_code) for the three impls, while the L2Bridge impl control returns abi + 28,487 chars of source; Sourcify returns 404 for the three impls with the same control present. Basescan unread (Cloudflare).

findings.title: Undocumented privileged + money interface on the Custodian and CurveBook
findings.impact: The docs publish a read ABI and describe the Custodian only as a read target, while the bytecode exposes deposit/requestWithdraw/claim/totalClaimable/withdrawDelay(600s)/initialize on the Custodian and initialize + eip712Domain on the CurveBook — i.e. a full maker custody lifecycle and a signing domain that integrators cannot see.
findings.evidence: interface_map.py: PUSH4 enumeration + 4byte resolution of 0x997b2D1B (Custodian) and 0xBfF02E9E (CurveBook).

findings.title: Both audit report links published in the docs return 404
findings.impact: docs/developers/audits.md lists an OpenZeppelin audit and a Sherlock report; both PDF URLs 404 as published, so a reader cannot retrieve the reports from the documentation.
findings.evidence: GET https://docs.baibai.cx/audits/openzeppelin-audit-1.pdf -> 404; .../sherlock-baibai-audit-report.pdf -> 404; alternate paths and mintcdn probes also 404 (2026-09-22).

positive_observations: L2Router.owner() = 0x28BAd3f4.. = the published L2BaibaiAdmin CONTRACT, not a bare EOA — good pattern on the verified side.
L2BaibaiAdmin is mid-migration from an EOA (0x5c55dd20..) to a 3-of-9 Safe (pendingOwner 0xe6419b6d..) — the team is actively hardening key management on the L2 side.
Entrypoint/CurveBook/Custodian wiring is internally consistent and matches the docs (entrypoint<->curveBook<->custodian cross-reads all agree; quoteToken = USDC on Base).
